lines.en: It’s a completely normal and peaceful day in my office.
Nevermind.
: Sir!
: What, Molly?
: The three of us require your assistance! Or...guidance! Or something!
: Why? Aren’t you supposed to be at your club right now?
: This actually...is our club activity for the day. We’re teaching Yasu about manga.
: I see.
: Just so we’re all on the same page here, you guys know I that I am pretty much entirely unfamiliar with manga, right?
: Aye!
: And that asking me for help with this is essentially pointless because of that.
: Aye!
: Okay, cool. I just wanted to make sure.
: So...you’ll come with us, then?
: I’m not sure. Why not leave my involvement up to Yasu? You know, since her new thing is apparently just ghosting on me without a care in the world.
: Ghost?
: Oof. That sort of crit would take most other people out in one shot, Sir. I’m surprised you’re still able to stand up after that.
: You and...Yasu have been spending time together?
: If by spending time with her you mean her offering me eggs and then immediately leaving in the middle of conversations, yes.
: That’s not...really what I meant, no.
: I’m sorry, but...I don’t remember this at all.
: You don’t remember having a “summer celebration” with a bunch of rabbit dolls in that weird cathedral and drinking tea made from back alley leaf litter?
: I remember the celebration, but I don’t remember your presence.
: Which made me very sad since I brewed extra tea for you.
: Wait...you...drank tea made of leaves you found on the ground?
: Special leaves that the one with many eyes blew onto the sacred asphalt behind the place He falls asleep at night.
: Are we going to ignore the “party with rabbit dolls” part? Or is that something we just expect out of her ghostliness at this point?
: Wait, Yasu- do you really not remember me being there?
: I waited so long for you that Touka sent one of her fancy cars to come pick me up so I wouldn’t have to walk home during what she called the “witching hour.”
: Now, you’ll have to wait until next summer for divine protection.
: Or just find yourself a paladin. Which, not gonna lie, is far easier said than done, Sir.
: I’ll be fine without “divine protection.” What I’m more concerned about is the fact that I now have memories of a thing that apparently never happened.
: Perhaps this is just some sort of dream you’re remembering, Sir? Yasu doesn’t seem like the type to cast vanish in the middle of casual conversation.
: Maybe. It’s just weird that I’d also remember the names of her stuffed rabbits.
: The rabbits do not belong to me. They belong to everyone.
: They are His ears...and carry forth the whispers too soft for Him to hear on His own.
: All shapes and all sizes.
: All forms and all colors.
: Except red.
: Red is bad.
: I take great offense to this.
: Well, I don’t really remember what colors or sizes they were...but does the name “Wormwood” ring a bell?
: Aye! That’s a card from the World of Warcraft TCG that allows you to put a target ally into-
: Yes! Wormwood is an emissary! One who carries all sorts of information about the history of the church!
: Yeah! Or that!
: I am glad you remember him!
: But I don’t understand how that would be possible. He only appears to me on special occasions and you were not at the celebration.
: I’m telling you I was, though...
: Did you drink the tea?
: No. I-
: You should have drank the tea. It is possible your body was detached from your mind as a result of your failure to do so.
Or it’s possible that Yasu is insane and simply doesn’t remember the fact that we had an entire conversation about her god at a table full of stuffed animals.
I guess that wouldn’t really explain the sudden vanishing of them, though...
But it’s entirely possible I just lost track of time again. It obviously wouldn’t be the first time something like that happened.
And it sure as hell makes a lot more sense than vanishing rabbits or the sudden introduction of “amnesia” to the list of mental issues Yasu likely needs to be professionally diagnosed with.
I do feel a little better knowing that there was no conscious decision to ghost me, though.
And I guess it’s fine to prioritize that over the idea of false memories because, let’s face it, I’ve become a bit of an expert when it comes to memory related issues.
Just don’t tell that to Maya or she’ll probably get sad and reflective.
: Yasu...I really don’t think you should be making tea out of things you find on the ground...
: You would change your mind if you had some. It is the cure for all things and would quell the sadness in your heart that eats away at your innards like carrion birds.
: The feeling you’re describing sounds...more like a virus you may have gotten from-
: Can we stop talking about carrion birds and tea leaves and get back to the topic at hand?
: We’re here to enlist Sensei’s help for Yasu’s reeducation process, aren’t we?
: Reeducation process?
: I am broken beyond repair and these two wonderful and helpful girls are going to help fix me.
: We’re not going to fix you, Yasu...We just want to help you figure out what type of manga you like since you’ve never read any and...have decided to join the manga club despite that.
: Shh. Stop. Don’t say anything that might make her question her decision. We need every member to stay in the club or we’ll all wind up in costumes at Sensei’s house.
: That sounds delightful.
: No...that sounds very embarrassing...
: As supportive as I am of the idea of everyone coming over to my house and putting on cosplay, I still don’t understand how I am supposed to help Yasu figure out what kind of manga she likes.
: Especially when I don’t even know what kind of manga I like.
: As the club advisor, that is probably something you should know, Sir.
: As the club president, you should be off doing your job instead of dragging me into it as well.
: But, Sir! If I’m not annoying you every hour of every day, what purpose do I even have?
: Have you been talking to Io lately?
: Sir. No one has been talking to Io lately.
: You know what? That’s fair.
: I like her hair. It reminds me of the grass.
: Sensei...the reason we need your help is less of an actual need for help and more the fact that...Yasu seemed upset that you weren’t going to be at club.
: What? Really?
: Summer can only do so much for the sounds I hear. Having you nearby makes them even clearer.
: Did you hear that, Sir? Are you really going to say no to a line as cute as that?
: Yes.
: Strike that. Are you really going to say no to a line as cute as that knowing that Yasu will also be in cosplay?
: In addition to wanting you there...Yasu was also upset that we weren’t dressing up today...
: See, this is a detail that should have been revealed from the start. This changes everything.
: I hope that you are not repulsed by the sight of a worm in beautiful clothing.
: If you are, just close your eyes. You need not see for me to feel your presence. But you must be present for me to see.
: Do you see?
: No. But I’m not about to try and figure it out when I know that something much more interesting than this awaits in the club room.
: Okay. Everybody out. Come on.
: Quest complete! Fantastic job, Yasu!
: Remind me to come up with a nickname for you as soon as possible. You’ve earned it.
: I have earned nothing but a life of servitude for-
: Oh, look. We’re here...
: Sensei...you can wait out here with me while Molly helps Yasu get changed...
: I hope you like crimson demons, Sir. Because what you’re about to see is bound to make you explode.
: Demon? But demons are bad. I don’t want to be a demon.
: Well...the name is more of a technicality than anything. The character is basically just a fire mage.
: But warlocks and mages are also enemies of God.
: Do you have anything with wings?
: Uhh...not on hand, no. But you’ll be fine. It’s just pretend, okay?
: Now, get in there and start stripping. We don’t want the Herald of the Adolescents waiting too long, do we?
Molly shoves Yasu into the club room and Futaba lets out a hearty sigh, showcasing just how exhausting the introduction of everyone’s favorite cult member to their friend group is.
She tells me a little about how she expected things to settle down after Rin left.
But apparently, having someone completely new to the nerd world around has awoken something in Molly that she is having trouble containing.
And while I’d like to talk about how I’m sure this is all just temporary and that Yasu will adjust and Molly will settle down in no time at all, both of those things are obviously untrue.
In fact, I can’t fathom any scenario where Yasu doesn’t stick out like a sore thumb.
But I’m glad she’s trying.
Even if her efforts are currently resulting in her being dragged around like a puppy on a leash by a small Irish girl.
Even before that, though, Yasu was already on a leash.
She probably has been for a very long time now.
We should be happy that we can see what this new one is attached to.
: Ta-dah! Yasumin!
: And it only took me one night to adjust the costume for her size!
: Yasu! Say the line!
: Boom!
: Close enough!
: I’m not sure if it lives up to the one from the dorm wars, but I accept and appreciate this greatly and thank all of you for allowing me to be involved.
: Don’t thank us, Sir! Thank Yasu for her ideal cosplay figure and extremely unique and only mildly creepy aesthetic.
: Do I look like a real manga character now?
: Sure. But with an extra dimension, which makes things even better.
: Debatable!
: So...have you thought at all about what genre you’d like to try first, Yasu?
: We have all different types of books here. Ami and Maya even brought in most of their collection for you to sort through if you’d like.
: I don’t know if Yasu’s ready for any of the stuff Maya reads. PunPun isn’t really entrance level material unless you’re looking to an-hero.
: What is entrance level material? I would like to stay away from anything with gratuitous violence or premarital sex.
: Okay. Well, that rules out pretty much Rin’s entire collection, so...let’s see what else we can find laying around here.
Molly and Futaba begin sorting through a few boxes while Yasu and I stand awkwardly in the corner, occasionally making eye contact- which may or may not be a sin according to her religion.

I take the fact that she hasn’t spontaneously burst into a fit of tears to be a good sign, though, and let the awkward silence bridge the ever growing gap between us in the form of a temporary respite.
There’s still a great deal I don’t understand about her. Particularly the parts where she vanishes and leaves me alone at a table full of eggs, but things like that can wait until another day.
For now, I’m just interested in seeing how she functions as a normal misfit girl, trying to fit in with people who genuinely want her to fit in-
And likely making everyone very uncomfortable in the process.
: Question! How gratuitous is “gratuitous violence?”
: Can there be any violence at all? Because there are a lot of very accessible shonen manga that serve as an awesome gateway to the world of anime!
: Umm...
: Is all romance off the table as well? Or just romantic series with...um...premarital sex?...
: Because romantic subplots are essentially impossible to avoid in fiction, but there are a lot of fantasy series I enjoy that barely focus on it at all. And I think you’d love those!
: That...sounds like it might be okay...
: What about this?

I pick up the first book I see on top of a stack that looks relatively safe for work. And after skimming through the pages, I can say with utmost certainty that there is no premarital sex or gratuitous violence.
It doesn’t really seem like there’s much of anything, though.
It’s just...people talking.
: Whatcha got there, Sir? You digging into Ami’s slice of life pile?
: Oh, I think something like that might be good for Yasu as well.
: Slice of life?
: I guess that’s what I’m holding, sure.
: It’s not violent?
: Not that kind of slice, Yasu.
: In fact, here’s a little weebnote for you.
: Slice of life is a genre of anime and manga that focuses primarily on the lives of the characters in the story and less on a unified and major coherent plotline.
: That’s not to say there’s never any sort of plot at all, though. A lot of SoL series can blend in action and drama without ever abandoning their roots.
: It’s something people tend to gravitate to after overloading themselves on more serious or action-packed series to sort of...unwind or reset.
: But that doesn’t mean you can’t start there! And the one Sensei is holding would actually be a great one to go with since I’ve already finished it and can confirm there is zero sex at all!
: Hooray for no inappropriate content!
: Yeah! Hooray, I guess!
: I still think you should maybe consider shonen, though, since a lot of it nowadays is-
: Just let her have this, Molly.
I hand the book over to Yasu, who accepts it with the least creepy smile I have seen out of her thus far.
She opens it up and begins reading very slowly, focusing for far too long on each and every page as if she’s taking in every last detail and every last line.
I’m sure that the artists involved would be happy to see this, but even then I think they’d believe it to be a tad excessive.
Molly and Futaba cross the room and take their places beside me like we’re some sort of proud, polyamorous couple watching our daughter take her first steps.
I’m just a little disappointed because her steps are in a direction that I’m not particularly interested or invested in.
But hey, this is the first time I’ve ever seen a smile like that out of her.
And it’s a lot more infectious than those that have been induced by her god.
Yasu continues reading until the sun begins to set while the rest of us talk quietly amongst ourselves.
When the final bell rings, Yasu closes her book and thanks all of us for our help.
But not before grabbing three more books of what I expect and hope are the same genre.
Yasu’s affection has increased to [yasu_love]!
